Scene/backdrop: Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation-inspired cool-temperate lake-margin and volcanic-ash plain in Liaoning, China at cold blue-gray dawn. Sparse irregular conifers, ginkgo-like trees, low ferns and horsetails, dark tuffaceous soil, faint lake mist and subdued distant volcanic terrain. This is cool volcanic terrain, NOT a snowfield. No falling snow, no blizzard, no ice-age landscape, no modern grass, no flowers.

Subject and head identity: one large but relatively lightly built basal tyrannosauroid, about 9 m long, with a large yet not extremely deep T. rex-like skull and one clearly visible large external naris. The skull roof must carry ONE rough but continuous LOW-TO-MODERATE median premaxillary-nasal ridge integrated into the skull profile. It may be gently uneven and rugose, but it must remain one connected ridge. Absolutely no separate triangular spikes, no serrated saw-tooth crest, no horn row, no paired horns, no plates, and no tall sail.

Composition/framing: landscape 3:2. Full animal visible from snout to tail tip in a calm front three-quarter / anterolateral view, approaching diagonally at a slow walk or standing alert. Keep the head, both arms and hands, both legs and feet, pelvis, and complete tail inside the frame with generous clearance. Stagger limbs naturally so every appendage and digit can be counted. The face and median ridge must be readable. Show a small natural plume of visible breath vapor at the nostrils or slightly parted mouth, but keep it translucent and away from the eye, naris, jawline, hands, and body silhouette.

Anatomy gates: exactly one head; exactly TWO well-developed forelimbs, distinctly longer and more functional than Tyrannosaurus rex arms; each hand must show exactly THREE separate, connected, clawed fingers, all six fingers readable and neither hand hidden against the chest. Exactly TWO strong hind limbs; both feet fully visible and grounded, each foot showing exactly THREE main forward weight-bearing toes, all six main toes readable. No enlarged raised dromaeosaur sickle claw. Exactly ONE long continuous balancing tail connected to the pelvis, uncut and untufted. No duplicated, fused, missing, hidden, or extra limbs, digits, heads, or tails.

Integument: extensive long, simple filamentous plumage across neck, torso, upper arms, thighs, and tail, reading as shaggy protofeathers. Keep individual filaments simple and hairlike without becoming mammalian fur. No modern pennaceous flight feathers, no bird wings, no spread wing fans, no tail fan, no porcupine quills, and no naked scaly T. rex body.

Color and pattern: preserve only the reference's broad hypothetical palette and proportions: ivory and cool ash-white long filaments broken by irregular soft-edged slate-gray and muted taupe mottling, with a lighter throat and belly. The pattern is an artistic hypothesis, not fossil color evidence. Avoid zebra stripes, regular rings, polka dots, panda mask, or featureless pure white.

Lighting/mood/style: cold diffuse dawn light, quiet documentary museum paleoart, realistic anatomy and materials, clear educational silhouette, approachable and non-aggressive. The visible breath establishes cold air without implying a permanent snowy climate.

Constraints: exactly one animal; no prey, no hunting, no attack, no carcass, no wounds, no blood, no other animals; no roaring monster pose; no text, caption, label, logo, border, signature, or watermark; do not imitate any named artist.

Critical reject conditions: any triangular or saw-toothed crest; any isolated spike or horn on the premaxilla/nasal midline; hidden or uncountable hands, fingers, feet, or toes; two-finger T. rex arms; bird wings or flight feathers; raised sickle claw; cropped tail; extra anatomy; snowfield or falling snow.

Keep exactly two animals total, both completely in frame. Preserve the compact pale breath plume emerging from the Yutyrannus nostrils and slightly open mouth, and keep it separate from both bodies.
